messages:
daria-cs: Heads-up: customer ACME Inc submitted a DPA erasure request via ticket #INC-12345. They want: 1) confirmation their EU-region data is removed, 2) whether rotating or deleting KMS keys satisfies 'erasure' for audit, and 3) a copy of audit logs showing access and deletion events. CC @tanvi-secbiz

tanvi-secbiz: Thanks @daria-cs — can you paste the customer's workspace id + request timestamp? Also flagging @omar-support to help on logs retrieval.

daria-cs: Workspace: eu-acme-prod (org id: org_0a1b2c). Request timestamp: 2026-02-15T09:12:00Z. Customer also asked: if we delete their data, can they still request a data export? :thinking_face:

omar-support: We can pull audit logs for that org. Two caveats: (a) if data was stored encrypted with a KMS key and we rotate/delete the key, ciphertext can't be decrypted, but that doesn't mean bytes are removed from object storage. (b) For DPA proof, customers usually need a combination: deletion confirmation + immutable audit showing deletion operation. I'll start the log pull.

tanvi-secbiz: Agree. Legal prefers a statement: 'we have deleted customer data from live systems and retained only minimal metadata in hashed form for X days under lawful purpose' — but for exports, if deleted, export cannot be produced. @mike-sre do we have a canonical wording?

mike-sre: We have a standard DPA response template. Short answer: key rotation alone != deletion of ciphertext from object store. Example log entries we can provide:

```
2026-02-15T09:13:01Z INFO DELETE_REQUEST user=redacted initiator=acme_admin resource=chat_messages workspace=eu-acme-prod request_id=req-9f2a
2026-02-15T09:13:05Z INFO OBJECT_DELETE key=objects/msgs/2026/02/15/xyz123 size=2.1KB storage=eu-west-1
2026-02-15T09:13:07Z INFO KMS_KEY_ROTATE key=kms-eu-1 old_key=k-111 new_key=k-222 initiated_by=infra-batch
```

omar-support: I'll attach pulled logs (filtered) to the ticket. Note: we redact PII and content fields. Customer asked about subprocessors: relevant ones are our cloud provider (GCP europe-west), S3-compatible storage provider, and managed KMS provided by our cloud partner. Will confirm the official list.

daria-cs: Customer expects formal statement listing subprocessors + confirmation that backups were purged. Any backup retention policies to note?

tanvi-secbiz: Backups: we retain encrypted backups for 30 days in EU regions, then rotate & expire. For DPA erasure, we perform an isolated expunge job and schedule backup purge within the retention window; we can provide timestamped proof of job completion.

mike-sre: I'll schedule the expunge run and capture job-id + logs. For the audit deliverable, legal likes: (1) copy of redacted audit log showing deletion, (2) statement on key handling (we never delete keys before confirming data removal), (3) subprocessor list & residency statement. ETA: 24-48h.

daria-cs: Thanks. Can we also confirm whether HSM-backed KMS (customer asked if keys were in HSM) is used for this org?

tanvi-secbiz: Our EU KMS is HSM-backed via cloud KMS (yes). Note: keys are service-managed for this hosted org; Dedicated/Private customers can bring their own keys (BYOK). We'll state that explicitly.

omar-support: Ticket update I'll post to customer: short non-technical summary + attached redacted logs and link to subprocessor list. @daria-cs want me to include the exact job log snippet when expunge completes?

daria-cs: Yes please. Keep it minimal and legal-approved lines only. I'll route final package through legal for sign-off.

legal-bot: Reminder: include coverage dates for subprocessor list and include the DPA clause reference. If customer requests a formal erasure certificate, escalate to legal@redwood.

daria-cs: Will do. Posting interim response to customer now. :thumbsup:
